sentences.text: A person climbs off a station platform onto the railway tracks.
Hafnia, watching this recording, answers:
no entry observed.
That answer is understandable.
The person sat at the edge for six seconds.
But in a security room, a no is silent.
Nobody looks again.
Adaptive Watch adds a second signal.
A person detector on a Linux A10G GPU watches the same recording for one configured condition:
someone at the platform edge.
It flagged the person almost four seconds before they climbed down.
Here is the mechanism.
XProtect records the scene.
Hafnia reads it.
The GPU detector watches it.
Adaptive Watch compares the two.
When Hafnia says no, but the detector sees the condition, it raises a review exception, and sends it back into XProtect.
The operator opens the exception at the moment that matters.
The detection, the watched region, and Hafnia's answer share one timeline over the original footage.
Play from the trigger, and the person reaches the track bed.
One click requests the XProtect review.
Sending it needs a second, explicit confirmation, and nothing is sent before that.
The same flow also ran live from the browser:
a fresh recording, one real Hafnia request, and the GPU detector.
Hafnia again answered not observed, and the detector placed the person at the edge.
XProtect receives the review event on the correct camera and raises its own alarm.
In the Smart Client, the live run's alarm opens the recorded footage with the detector box.
The saved case's 22 October recording is past retention, so that alarm cannot replay it.
Three systems, three jobs.
XProtect records, and owns the alarm.
Hafnia reads the scene.
A local GPU detector watches for a rule.
During the hackathon we built the detector pipeline, the comparison, the review interface, and the XProtect handoff.
A negative AI assessment no longer has to be the end of the review.
The evidence comes from controlled synthetic camera scenarios.
It is not an accuracy benchmark.

proof: Smart Client, 28 Oct, after a client restart: live and recorded playback of the camera verified; alarm 5 preview shows the footage and box.
